title: At BATS, the 26.4-26.6 layer had higher AOU concentration but a smaller AOU inventory in 2016-2025 than in 1989-1998
abstract: At BATS, we tested whether the rise of apparent oxygen utilization (AOU) near sigma-theta 26.5 means that its density layer holds more total oxygen deficit. We integrated oxygen and AOU across 26.4-26.6 in bottle profiles from 1989-2025. Between 1989-1998 and 2016-2025, mean layer AOU rose by 11.50 umol/kg, while thickness fell by 76.88 m and the AOU inventory fell by 0.99 mol/m2 (95% three-year block interval -1.72 to -0.19). The exact inventory split is +2.14 mol/m2 from concentration and -3.13 from thickness. An unchanged deficit in the thinner layer would give 52.15 umol/kg, above the measured 45.40, so the conserved-deficit end-member fails under these assumptions. Oxygen inventory fell by 17.31 mol/m2; the thickness accounting term is 88.5% of that fall. A 200 m gap rule and no seasonal adjustment give the same signs. Adjacent layers have higher AOU but no resolved inventory change. The strict interpolation rule has insufficient data. This local result gives a joint concentration and inventory target for a model with changing layer volume. It does not identify respiration or close the flux budget. The intervals exclude measurement and interpolation errors.

display.caption: BATS layer AOU, thickness and integrated deficit. Grey bands mark 1989-1998 and 2016-2025. Accounting terms in panel D have 95% circular three-year block intervals. They are not independent causes.
